name: Prompt Injection & LLM Input Manipulation
description: Assessment of LLM-integrated applications against manipulation of model inputs and unsafe handling of model outputs. Covers direct and indirect prompt injection, system-prompt extraction, improper output handling that turns model output into downstream injection (OWASP LLM01, LLM05, LLM07), and the design and evaluation of guardrails and input/output filters. Jailbreak and harm-elicitation campaigns belong to AIML-LLM-REDTEAM; tool-use and agent privilege issues belong to AIML-LLM-AGENT.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to prompt injection or LLM input manipulation

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands why LLMs cannot reliably separate instructions from data
evidence: Can explain direct versus indirect prompt injection and why it differs from classic injection flaws
Aware of system-prompt leakage and improper output handling risks (OWASP LLM01, LLM05, LLM07)
Familiar with common guardrail approaches such as input classifiers, output filters, and instruction hierarchy

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Can execute known prompt injection techniques under guidance
evidence: Demonstrates direct prompt injection and system-prompt extraction against a lab application
Plants indirect injection payloads in documents, web pages, or e-mails consumed by the application
Identifies model output rendered unsafely downstream (HTML, Markdown, SQL, shell) with supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses LLM applications for input manipulation and output handling flaws
evidence: Maps every untrusted input channel into the prompt context, including retrieved and third-party content
Demonstrates impact chains from injection to data exfiltration, for example via Markdown image or link rendering
Measures guardrail and filter bypass rates using obfuscation, encoding, and multi-turn techniques
Produces findings with reproducible payloads, success rates, and layered mitigations

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex LLM applications; develops injection test methodology; mentors others
evidence: Develops novel indirect injection vectors for new input modalities such as images, audio, and files
Builds automated injection test suites integrated into application CI pipelines
Evaluates architectural defences such as privilege separation, dual-LLM patterns, and output sanitisation
Reviews and calibrates prompt injection assessments across the team

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's prompt injection assessment practice; publishes research
evidence: Established the lab's methodology for prompt injection and output handling assessment
Published research on prompt injection attacks, defences, or guardrail evaluation
Trains teams on LLM input manipulation assessment
Contributes to external guidance such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications

assessment_methods.description: Against a lab LLM application with document ingestion, achieve system-prompt extraction and an indirect injection that exfiltrates data through rendered output
Review a prompt injection assessment report for input-channel coverage, reproducible payloads, measured bypass rates, and layered mitigations
